name: org.machanism.machai:ghostwriter
description: Ghostwriter is a Java command-line and embeddable project automation engine in the Machai ecosystem. It scans software projects, source code, tests, documentation, Maven site pages, diagrams, configuration files, and other repository artifacts; extracts embedded @guidance instructions; builds project-aware prompts; and dispatches them to a configured GenAI provider. It also supports reusable TOML-based Acts with inheritance, episodes, interactive sessions, project context variables, controlled file operations, safe command execution, web and REST access, and asynchronous workflow execution. The artifact is useful for repository-wide AI-assisted documentation generation, code documentation, guided file processing, CI/CD automation, project maintenance, vulnerability remediation workflows, SonarQube issue fixing workflows, unit-test generation workflows, and governed repeatable automation where instructions live in version-controlled project files.

classification.type: command-line application, AI automation library, project processing tool
usageContext: Run as a CLI using gw.jar to process files, folders, glob patterns, or regex patterns in a project repository.
Run in Act mode to execute reusable TOML prompt workflows with optional episodes and interactive continuation.
Embed processor classes in Java tooling to scan projects and dispatch guidance-aware prompts to GenAI providers.
Use in CI/CD pipelines to update documentation, apply repository maintenance guidance, generate code documentation, or execute repeatable AI-assisted project tasks.
Use as a host-integrated function-tool provider for file, command, web, REST, act, guidance, and project-context operations.

features.name: Ghostwriter CLI entry point
features.signature: public static void org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.Ghostwriter.main(java.lang.String[] args) throws java.io.IOException, org.apache.commons.cli.ParseException
features.description: Starts the Ghostwriter command-line application. The CLI accepts project-relative paths, raw directories, glob patterns, and regex patterns; supports options for project directory, model, threads, instructions, excludes, input logging, acts directory, and Act mode; and then dispatches either guidance processing or Act processing for the selected target.

examples.snippet: java -jar gw.jar src/main/java -d . -m OpenAI:gpt-5.1 -t 4 -e ".git,target" -i "Use concise Javadoc and preserve public API behavior." -l
examples.description: Runs the ready-to-use CLI against src/main/java, configures the project root, selects a model, enables four processing threads, excludes build and VCS folders, supplies extra instructions, and logs provider inputs.

features.name: Guidance tag processing
features.signature: public java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.GuidanceProcessor.process(org.machanism.machai.project.layout.ProjectLayout projectLayout, java.io.File file, java.lang.String guidance)
features.description: Composes standard Ghostwriter instructions with file-specific or fallback guidance and sends the request to the configured AI provider. This is the main feature for converting embedded @guidance comments and @guidance.txt files into repeatable project automation.

examples.snippet:
<!-- @guidance:
Rewrite this Markdown page for first-time users. Keep the language simple, preserve existing command examples, and add one practical scenario.
-->
examples.description: A practical Markdown guidance block. When Ghostwriter scans the file, the Markdown reviewer extracts the block and GuidanceProcessor uses it to update the file through the configured provider.

features.name: Act loading and execution
features.description: Loads an Act definition by name or TOML path, merges inherited values, applies configuration options, injects the optional user prompt, and prepares execution. Acts support built-in and custom definitions, basedOn inheritance, $$super.value$$ merging, episodes, prologue and epilogue acts, interactive mode, model overrides, path filters, and tool-enabled workflows.

examples.snippet: gw --act code-doc Document public classes and methods in the service layer
examples.description: Runs the built-in code-doc Act from the CLI and passes a practical prompt describing the documentation scope.

features.name: Episode workflow sequencing
features.description: Executes Act episode prompts in natural order while supporting repeat and move-to-episode control flow. Episodes can also be selected explicitly by one-based ID or heading name so complex workflows can be split into clear steps such as analysis, generation, validation, and registration.

examples.description: Runs only episodes 1 and 3 of a multi-episode Act and stops after the selected episodes because of the exclamation suffix.

features.name: Reviewer SPI
features.signature: public java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer.perform(java.io.File projectDir, java.io.File file) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Defines the service-provider contract for file-type-specific guidance extraction. Implementations understand comment styles for Java, Markdown, HTML, XML, Python, TypeScript, PlantUML, and @guidance.txt files and return normalized prompt fragments for Ghostwriter processing.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer reviewer = new org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.JavaReviewer();
java.lang.String promptFragment = reviewer.perform(new java.io.File("."), new java.io.File("src/main/java/example/App.java"));
examples.description: Uses the Java reviewer directly to extract a guidance prompt fragment from a Java source file containing @guidance in line or block comments.

features.name: File function tools
features.signature: public java.lang.Object org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.FileFunctionTools.readFile(java.lang.String filePath, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Provides host-integrated file tools for reading, writing, patching, and listing project files relative to a controlled project directory. These tools are exposed to AI workflows so Acts can inspect and update repository files safely.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.FileFunctionTools tools = new org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.FileFunctionTools();
java.lang.Object content = tools.readFile("pom.xml", "UTF-8", new java.io.File("."));
examples.description: Reads the project pom.xml through the file tool API using a project-relative path.

features.name: Command execution tools
features.signature: public java.lang.Object org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.CommandFunctionTools.executeCommand(java.lang.String command, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> properties, java.lang.String dir, int tailResultSize, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Executes approved system commands in a project-relative working directory with environment overrides, bounded output capture, command-log persistence, and deny-list security checks. This enables build, test, status, and diagnostic commands in automated Acts.

examples.description: A typical command invoked through Ghostwriter command tools during an Act to validate generated code or tests.

features.name: Act function tools
features.signature: public java.lang.Object org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.ActFunctionTools.performAct(java.lang.String actName, java.io.File projectDir, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> properties, boolean async, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator config) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Loads and performs a named Act either synchronously or asynchronously. Asynchronous runs return a process identifier and store results for later retrieval, making it possible to orchestrate long-running project automation from tool-enabled prompts.

examples.description: Runs the code-doc Act synchronously for Java files and passes a path override through the properties map.

features.name: Web and REST tools
features.signature: public java.lang.String org.machanism.machai.gw.tools.WebFunctionTools.callRestApi(java.lang.String url, java.lang.String method, java.util.Map<java.lang.String,java.lang.String> headers, java.lang.String body, int timeout, java.lang.String charsetName, java.io.File projectDir, org.machanism.macha.core.commons.configurator.Configurator configurator) throws java.io.IOException
features.description: Calls HTTP or REST endpoints with method, headers, body, timeout, charset, and Basic authentication support through URL userInfo. Header placeholders such as ${sonar.token} are resolved at runtime by the configurator, enabling secure integrations with external services such as SonarQube without hard-coding credentials.

examples.description: Calls a SonarQube REST endpoint using runtime-resolved placeholders. The placeholders must remain unchanged in source configuration and are substituted only at execution time.

customizations.name: Custom Act TOML files
customizations.description: Developers can create TOML Act definitions with instructions, inputs, description, basedOn inheritance, gw.path, gw.threads, gw.excludes, gw.nonRecursive, gw.interactive, gw.model, and other configuration keys. Acts may be loaded from bundled resources, a custom directory, a remote acts location, or an absolute TOML file path. Placeholder variables in the ${...} format are resolved at runtime and must not be modified in source templates.

customizations.name: Reviewer implementations
customizations.description: Developers can add file-format-specific guidance extraction by implementing the Reviewer SPI and providing supported extensions and extraction logic. This extends Ghostwriter to additional source, documentation, configuration, or domain-specific file formats.

examples.description: Skeleton for a custom reviewer that could extract @guidance content from a project-specific file format.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer
studs.description: Service-provider interface for components that scan project files and extract @guidance instructions for downstream Ghostwriter processing. Implementations return a formatted prompt fragment or null when no actionable guidance exists.

examples.snippet:
org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.Reviewer reviewer = new org.machanism.machai.gw.reviewer.MarkdownReviewer();
java.lang.String[] extensions = reviewer.getSupportedFileExtensions();
examples.description: Uses a built-in Reviewer implementation to inspect supported extensions for Markdown guidance extraction.

studs.name: org.machanism.machai.gw.processor.AbstractFileProcessor
studs.description: Base implementation for processors that traverse a project directory, apply path matching and exclusions, support module recursion, and delegate per-file work to subclasses. It is the boundary for building new filesystem-oriented project processors.

examples.description: Shows how a custom processor can extend the common traversal foundation used by Ghostwriter processors.

examples.title: Install and run the Ghostwriter CLI pack
examples.scenario: Use Ghostwriter as a ready-to-run command-line application for guided documentation or source processing.
steps: Download the Ghostwriter CLI delivery pack from https://sourceforge.net/projects/machanism/files/machai/ghostwriter/gw.zip/download.
Unpack the archive so gw.jar is available on your workstation or CI runner.
Configure provider credentials and defaults in gw.properties or pass runtime options on the command line.
Run java -jar gw.jar "glob:**/*.java" -d . -m OpenAI:gpt-5.1 to process Java files in the current project.
Review generated changes in version control before committing.
examples.description: This scenario demonstrates installation, configuration, and invocation of the standalone CLI component in a real project.

examples.title: Run an Act workflow
examples.scenario: Use a reusable prompt workflow for code documentation.
steps: Choose a built-in Act such as code-doc, commit, task, unit-tests, sonar-fix, grype-fix, or help.
Optionally configure a custom acts location with -as ./acts or the gw.acts property.
Invoke the Act with java -jar gw.jar . --act "code-doc Document only public API types".
For an interactive Act, type . to terminate the session or > to continue normal processing.
examples.description: Acts package common workflows as TOML templates so they can be reused locally and in CI/CD automation.

examples.description: The project build uses Ghostwriter Maven tooling and related Machai modules. Maven users can configure plugin versions and execution parameters in pom.xml as part of repository automation.
